fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. The text says the people "…gathered in such large numbers that there was no more room, not even outside the door…" (Mark 2:2) So there was no room left, even outside the door. And Jesus was speaking the word to them.
That's it, friend. "When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic…" (Mark 2:5) The text says their faith, and Jesus saw it. Then He spoke to the man on the mat.
Nope, friend. Nothing in the text points to pride. It says "When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic…" (Mark 2:5) Faith is what Jesus saw.
That's not what Jesus says here, friend. In Mark 2:5 He says, "Son, your sins are forgiven." Nothing about a priest shows up in His words. He starts with forgiveness.

That's right, friend. The scribes are thinking in their hearts, "Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?" (Mark 2:6-7) Their question is a good one, and Jesus is about to answer it.

Fair guess, friend, but that's not in this passage. The scribes think, "He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?" (Mark 2:7) The Sabbath isn't mentioned here, and what they're thinking is about forgiveness.

Yes, friend. "At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves." (Mark 2:8) He knew it right away. Then He asked them, "Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?" (Mark 2:8)

Silence can say a lot, friend, but this wasn't a guess. "At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves." (Mark 2:8) The text says He knew it, not that He guessed. He knew it right away, and He knew it in His spirit.

That's the one, baker! Jesus says, "But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins..." (Mark 2:10) "Son of Man" is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). So the reason He gives is His authority to forgive sins.

Elijah is a fine name to know, friend, but Jesus doesn't say it here. He says, "But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins..." (Mark 2:10) The point is His authority to forgive.

Right, friend. "…immediately the man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of them all." (Mark 2:12) No waiting and no helping hand. I'd have needed a minute and a cookie, but he stood right up.
Yes, friend. The text says "…they were all astounded…" (Mark 2:12) The man walked out in front of them all. And they said, "We have never seen anything like this!"

Not this one, friend. The text says "…they were all astounded and glorified God…" (Mark 2:12) It doesn't say they doubted. After the man walked out in front of them all, what the text says is astounded and glorified God.
